text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Vytautas Landsbergis, the parliament chairman and leader of the Homeland Union party, is the most popular person in Lithuania in 1996, according to an opinion poll by the Baltic Surveys. Landsbergis is closely followed by Algirdas Brazauskas, Lithuanian president, and Arvydas Sabonis, a basketball star, currently playing in NBA.
- Twenty percent of Lithuanians think 1996 has been successful for the country, 34 percent think it was unsuccessful and 40 percent were undecided, an opinion poll shows.
- The most important event in Lithuania in 1996 according to an opinion poll was the parliament election and the event of the year elsewhere in the world was the war in Chechnya.
- Alvydas Budrys of the state supervision body is expected to be appointed the new head of the customs department.
- The Lithuanian energy system is headed for crisis, Economy minister Vincas Babilius says in an interview, adding that it could be averted by decentralising and privatising the energy sector.
- A Lithuanian is among the group of 16 suspected of killing six Red Cross personnel on December 17 in Chechnya. The 30-year-old carries the passport of a Kaunas resident.
- The Lithuaninan trade deficit for the first nine months of 1996 was 2.78 billion litas.

- The Lithuaninan Gas companny promises there will be no radical increases in tariffs next year following the agreement on gas deliveries signed with the Russian Gazprom on conditions similar to those of last year.
- Lithuaninan Central Bank says the State Commercial bank saw its deposits decrease to 583 million litas in November compared to 578.4 million in September.
